name: BEL FUSE CLASS A

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The same counter the last pass faced and the right one to keep testing: that I should not 'fix' a count that may be correct by design — the LXP discipline, where a price that looked like the documented stock-split defect turned out to be handled properly and the lesson was that a prior lesson is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. The specific form here is that BELFA is a separately listed security with its own price, its own ticker and its own reported earnings per share, so valuing the Class A line on the Class A count is arguably the correct treatment rather than an error.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The Q3-26 release's own share and per-share tables, read directly, and the balance sheet behind them.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, and it defeats the counter on both limbs, now with fresher evidence than the last pass had. First, even taken on its own terms the figure is wrong for Class A: the engine uses 2,174,912 while the company reports Class A basic weighted-average shares of 2,115 thousand in all four periods of the Q3 release, because the 2011 figure predates fifteen years of treasury activity. Second, and decisive, the numerator is consolidated: there is one enterprise value, one cash balance, one FCFF base and one $609.7M of nine-month sales behind both tickers, and the release reports Class A and Class B earnings per share side by side off that single pool. Dividing the whole company's enterprise value by 15% of its shares is not a defensible per-class treatment, it is a units error. The free cross-check is the same impossible-turnover tell recorded on MIR: $21.9M of average daily dollar volume against a claimed $407.2M market capitalisation is 5.4% of the company changing hands every day, every day, which does not happen.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The size and funding of the remaining 20% Enercon buy-in, which is the second consecutive pass to leave it open. The company has not quantified it, carries it as an intention rather than a contractual obligation, and the XBRL dates it to 2027-01-01 — so it is a claim sitting in neither total_debt nor the share count, the PRM pattern, and on a corrected ~$3.30bn market capitalisation I still cannot say whether it is material. I also did not obtain a Q3 cash flow statement (the newest 10-Q is the 2026-08-04 half-year filing), so the FCFF base itself is unverified against current cash generation — though that is moot while the denominator is broken.

what_changed: The Q3-26 release of 2026-10-28 is new since the 2026-10-16 pass on this ticker, and it both confirms the defect and shows the business is performing well. Net sales $220.5M, up 23.2% year over year, with nine months at $609.7M, up 22.1% — and because Enercon closed on 2024-11-14 (agreement 2024-09-18), the prior-year comparative already contains it, so this growth is not the acquisition artifact the EFOR detector looks for. That answers one of the two items the last devil's advocate left open. Q4-26 is guided to $220-240M of net sales at 40.0-42.0% gross margin. The release also prints the decisive share-count evidence directly and by class: Class A basic weighted-average 2,115 thousand in every one of the four periods shown, Class B basic weighted-average 12,312 thousand against 10,548 a year earlier — a 16.7% increase that is the May 2026 underwritten offering of 1,725,000 Class B shares at $266.00. Earnings per share are reported separately for the two classes ($1.74 Class A and $1.84 Class B for the quarter, $4.45 and $4.69 for nine months), which is the clearest possible statement that both are claims on one pool of consolidated earnings with a fixed differential, not two companies. The second open item is NOT resolved: the remaining 20% of Enercon is still unquantified, still described as an intention rather than a sized obligation ('the possibility that Bel's intended acquisition of the remaining 20% stake in Enercon is not completed'), and the XBRL carries it as a forecast dated 2027-01-01. The staleness flag has moved from 5,555 days to 5,569 — i.e. fourteen days have passed and nothing has been fixed.
consensus_case: There is no price to steelman here, because the engine is not pricing Bel Fuse. It divides a CONSOLIDATED enterprise value by 2,174,912 shares — a Class A count taken from a 10-Q/A dated 2011-08-01, now 5,569 days stale — when the company's own Q3-26 release reports Class A basic weighted-average shares of 2,115 thousand AND Class B basic weighted-average shares of 12,312 thousand. The economic count is 14,427,000 and the engine is using 15% of it. What the market is actually paying for, on the real count, is a business growing fast: Q3-26 net sales of $220.5M against $179.0M, up 23.2%; nine-month net sales of $609.7M against $499.5M, up 22.1%; and fourth-quarter guidance of $220-240M at a 40.0-42.0% gross margin. Valuing each class at its own last price, the economic market capitalisation is about $3.30bn (2,115,000 Class A at $187.21 is $396M, plus 12,312,000 Class B at $235.73 is $2,902M), against the $407.2M on the face of this brief. The +189.8% gap and the 98th percentile of 125 Information Technology names are therefore not a statement about Bel Fuse at any price.
base_case_rationale: No growth rate can be supplied, because the number it would be applied to per share is wrong by a factor of about seven and the schema cannot correct it. The defect is arithmetic and total, not a matter of degree: the enterprise value, the cash, the debt and the $77.1M FCFF base are all CONSOLIDATED figures for the whole of Bel Fuse, and dividing them by one class's share count — itself the wrong figure for that class — is a category error regardless of which class happens to be listed under this ticker. The engine reports an enterprise value of $101.1M and an FCFF yield of 76.3% for a company that sold $609.7M of product in nine months; on the economic count the enterprise value is roughly $3.1bn. Per the YOU and SFBS discipline, supplying a final_growth here would publish a per-share fair value several times too high, which is worse than recording no number at all.
key_risks: shares_asof is 2011-08-01, now 5,569 days stale, and is a Class A figure only: 2,174,912 used against a reported 2,115,000 Class A plus 12,312,000 Class B = 14,427,000 economic shares
Economic market capitalisation is about $3.30bn against the brief's $407.2M (8.1x); the reported enterprise value of $101.1M and FCFF yield of 76.3% are arithmetic consequences of the error

The identical wrong count is served to BELFB in the SAME screen, producing a +138.1% gap on the same company against BELFA's +189.8% — the 52-point difference is nothing but the price spread between the two share classes
The May 2026 Class B offering was struck at $266.00 and Class B now trades at $235.73, about 12% below, five months later
The remaining 20% Enercon buy-in is unquantified, is forecast for 2027-01-01, and sits in neither total_debt nor the share count

The 'debt_likely_understated' flag inverts the diagnosis for the third recorded time after VISN and QTWO — total_debt of 0.0 is correct following the repayment of $197.5M from the offering proceeds, and the stale input is interest_expense
watch_for: A corrected, both-class share count in the extract — until then BELFA and BELFB will keep re-qualifying near the 98th percentile and consuming two opportunistic slots for one company, which is exactly what happened today
The size and funding of the remaining 20% Enercon stake, now dated to around 2027-01-01
Whether the 22% nine-month sales growth and the 40-42% guided gross margin hold into 2027, which is what would make the name worth re-screening once the denominator is fixed
